---
title: "phit"
---

Fit statistical models, compute probability distributions, and summarize data in PHP. Model functions accept formulas or explicit designs and return fit objects that print like R's and read like arrays.

Formulas follow R: `mpg ~ wt + factor(cyl)` models fuel economy from weight and the number of cylinders. phit builds the numeric design from named columns, including factors, interactions, and transformations such as `log(wt)`. `echo $fit` prints the fit as R does.

```php
use Phibble\DataFrame;

use function Phit\fit_ols;

$cars = DataFrame::fromCsv(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/datasets/main/csv/mtcars.csv',
);

$fit = fit_ols('mpg ~ wt + factor(cyl)', $cars);
echo $fit;
```

```
Linear model fit by least squares
Formula: mpg ~ wt + factor(cyl)

Coefficients:
             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept)   33.9908     1.8878  18.006  < 2e-16
wt            -3.2056     0.7539  -4.252 0.000213
factor(cyl)6  -4.2556     1.3861  -3.070 0.004718
factor(cyl)8  -6.0709     1.6523  -3.674 0.000999

Residual standard error: 2.557 on 28 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared: 0.8374, Adjusted R-squared: 0.82
F-statistic: 48.08 on 3 and 28 DF, p-value: 3.594e-11
```

[A first model](getting-started.qmd) walks through a fit, its result, and prediction on the same data.

## Capabilities

[All functions](functions/index.qmd) lists every function with its purpose and links to its reference entry.

| Area | Functions | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linear and generalized linear models | `fit_ols()`, `fit_generalized_linear()`: linear, logistic, probit, and Poisson regression with weights and offsets | [Models](models.qmd) |
| Mixed models | `fit_mixed_gaussian()` with random intercepts and slopes; `fit_mixed_logistic()` with one random intercept | [Mixed models](mixed-models.qmd) |
| Prediction | `predict()` on new data, with confidence and prediction intervals | [Model formulas](formulas.qmd#prediction-predict) |
| Distributions | Densities, CDFs, survival functions, and quantiles for 12 families (13 parameterizations) | [Probability distributions](distributions.qmd) |
| Seeded sampling | Reproducible draws, including uniform, categorical, and permutation sampling | [Seeded sampling](rng.qmd) |
| Descriptive statistics | Means, variances, quantiles, weighted statistics, kernel densities, and the ECDF | [Descriptive statistics](descriptive.qmd) |
| Posterior draws | Weighted moments and transforms for MCMC output | [Posterior draws](draw-numerics.qmd) |
| CSV input | A native reader, used by phibble | [Reading CSV files](io.qmd) |

Each model also has a matrix function, such as `fit_ols_matrix()`, for code that builds its own design. See [Model contracts](reference-models.qmd).

## Results

- Coefficient names, treatment contrasts, term order, deviance, and AIC follow R's `lm()` and `glm()`. Mixed models follow lme4.
- Rows with missing values are dropped with a warning, and every result reports which rows it used.
- Errors are PHP exceptions with stable numeric codes.
- The [verification](https://phit.phpstats.org/verification) pages compare each model with R, lme4, and statsmodels and record the tolerances.

## Requirements

phit runs on non-thread-safe PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5 on Linux and macOS. It installs with PIE or from prebuilt Linux binaries ([Installation](installation.qmd)). Where the extension cannot be installed, the plain-PHP [polyfill](extension-or-polyfill.qmd) provides every function except the CSV reader, and runs more slowly.
